Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/auth.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“"Two doors, in order: prove who you are (401), then prove your kitchen exists (409/redirect)."”

IStoken verification (Gustify's own Firebase project), the request auth context, the setup/consent gate (D148 server-side), the setup wizard + guard routing, and cross-user cache isolation (PersistGate + the signOut teardown).
IS NOTconsent RECORDS and account export/erasure — the legal-consent entity owns capture, storage, and the data rights; this entity owns the GATE that demands consent before a household exists.
DECIDES401 vs 403 vs "setup required" (409 on API, redirect on web); when a household comes into existence (exactly once, complete_setup); what dies at signOut (everything cached, in order).

a members-only workshop — the badge reader at the street door (token verify), the front desk that opens your workshop bay exactly once after you sign the waiver (setup + consent gate), and the locker room rule that your locker is emptied and re-keyed the moment you leave (PersistGate + teardown).

AnalogyIn this codebase
badge readerapps/api/auth/verifier.py:103-120
front deskapps/api/services/setup.py:337-407
the waiver checkservices/setup.py:364-374
locker re-keyapps/web/src/app/PersistGate.tsx:11-16, apps/web/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx:64-80

Easy to confuse:

  • the two 409s at setup — "setup in progress" (concurrent first-run) vs "consent required" (D148 gate); same status, different doors.
  • require_household()'s 409 "setup required" with an auth failure — the user IS authenticated; their kitchen doesn't exist yet.

Where the analogy stops working: the workshop analogy breaks at deletion — the badge is revoked LAST (post-commit Firebase delete), and a failure there still returns 204: the row wipe is the truth, the badge a best-effort cleanup.

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

Every request enters through build_auth_context (auth/context.py:64-87): the bearer token verified by Gustify's own Firebase project (blocking SDK call moved off the event loop, verifier.py:103-120; provider-switchable with mock forbidden in prod, D29/D33), the user resolved-or-created on first sight, and the household context loaded read-only — a household is NEVER auto-created (D35). Household-scoped routes call ctx.require_household() → HTTP 409 "setup required" (context.py:52-56); the web mirrors it as guard topology: RequireAuth (pending→splash, anon→/login?returnTo) then RequireSetup (setup_required→/setup, with /setup as a SIBLING so no redirect loop is possible). The household is born in exactly one place — complete_setup (services/setup.py:337-407): idempotency-keyed with REPLAY/IN_PROGRESS states, an already-set-up user gets their existing graph back (never an overwrite), and the D148 defense-in-depth sits AFTER the replay short-circuit and INSIDE the try — ConsentRequiredError (→409) when no current-version consent row exists, rolling back AND discarding the idempotency claim so a retry after accepting is a fresh claim, not a poisoned one. A direct-API caller cannot provision a household without accepting Privacy + Terms; programmatic seeds use ensure_consent to satisfy the same gate. On the web, identity is a tri-state (pending | authed | anon, authContext.ts:17) so a returning user never flashes login; and cross-user cache isolation is three-layered (PersistGate.tsx:11-16): a uid-namespaced IndexedDB store, a uid-keyed remount, and a synchronous cache clear on uid transition — completed by the load-bearing signOut teardown order (AuthProvider.tsx:64-80): cancel queries → clear cache → wipe the outgoing uid's persisted blob → clear cooking/local-modes residue → firebaseSignOut LAST, with a storm guard collapsing terminal-401 cascades into one sign-out.

For Whom

  • Every user — the badge check they never see; the setup wizard they see exactly once; the guarantee that a shared tablet never shows them someone else's pantry.
  • The household on one device — user B signs in after user A: B's cache is empty, A's blob is gone, nothing bleeds (the headline safety test, PersistGate.test.tsx).
  • The direct-API caller / attacker — cannot conjure a household without consent (D148), cannot replay a setup into an overwrite, cannot use a stale token (verify failures → 401, terminal-401s → clean sign-out).
  • The e2e/sandbox seeds — ensure_consent exists so programmatic users satisfy the same gate instead of bypassing it.

Flows

  • verify ★ → bearer token → FirebaseTokenVerifier (off-loop) → AuthContext {user, household?, membership?, principal_location?}; InvalidTokenError → 401; SSE variant reads a capped query-param token (EventSource cannot set headers, REQ-10). (assured: test_auth_context, 10 cases)
  • gate → household-scoped routes: require_household() → 409 "setup required"; web mirror: RequireAuth → RequireSetup → /setup sibling topology (no loop by construction). (assured: test_setup_routes; settings-auth journey — the P87 stale-session 401 fix — 3 e2e cases)
  • setup → POST /setup/complete (Idempotency-Key required): consent gate (D148, 409 consent-required) → household + primary_cook membership + principal Despensa + all preference upserts + completion stamp; replay returns the graph; failure rolls back AND discards the claim. GET /me serves setup_required. (assured: test_setup_service + test_setup_preferences_models, 20 cases)
  • wizard → the 8-step InitialSetupScreen (welcome…permissions) mapped by setupMapping.ts — allergens filtered to the offered set + capped, schema-validated locally so a mapping bug fails before the wire; the redo path preloads declared allergens so re-onboarding can never silently wipe them (C2). ConsentGate renders INSTEAD of the wizard until accepted (legal-consent owns the gate UI's content). Since P5b the wizard offers only the household modes it can HONOUR: householdModeOptions() gates "Tengo invitación" behind HOUSEHOLD_JOIN_ENABLED (false — no join flow exists), and the step renders FROM that list instead of two hardcoded cards, so a mode cannot appear without being offered (C4/D184; assured: C1142v2 + C8109).
  • isolate → uid change or signOut: the three PersistGate layers + the ordered teardown; onIdTokenChanged (wider than auth-state — fires on the ~1h refresh) keeps the API client's token getter fresh. (assured: PersistGate.test.tsx 8 cases + AuthProvider.signOut/authFailure tests + the persist/persisterRegistry resilience suite)
  • depart → DELETE /me: capture uid/ids BEFORE the wipe, delete_account + commit, THEN Firebase identity delete — a post-commit identity failure logs loudly and still 204s (the erasure semantics are legal-consent's card; the ordering is this entity's).

Is

  • One identity shape: VerifiedIdentity (provider, provider_id, email, display_name) — the app never touches raw Firebase claims outside the verifier.
  • Household existence is explicit: has_setup = household is not None; nothing auto-creates it; /me.setup_required is the single client-facing flag.
  • Consent is enforced server-side (D148): the gate lives in the setup service, not the client — the ConsentGate UI is the happy path, the 409 is the wall.
  • The signOut order is load-bearing: cancel → clear → wipe blob → residue → firebaseSignOut last; reversing any pair reopens a leak window (the test asserts the exact order, C1160).
  • Startup fail-fast: ensure_verifier_ready validates the service-account credential at boot, not at first request.
  • an invitation card that forks a household anyway — picking "Tengo invitación" produced a byte-identical setup DTO to "Crear hogar", so someone who thought they were joining a shared kitchen got their own empty one. Hidden until a join flow exists (D184), with the re-enable checklist written at the flag itself, not only in a decision file.

Is Not

  • not consent records/versioning, not export, not erasure content — legal-consent's card; the boundary is the GATE vs the RECORD.
  • not authorization beyond the household — there are no roles beyond primary_cook membership today; IDOR guards live in each domain's services.
  • not a session store — the server keeps no session state; identity is re-verified per request from the token.

Docs Changelog — decisions that shaped it

why the entity behaves the way it does

Source: the entity card's DECIDED section. A decision here is a rule the code obeys, not a plan — the ones with ids are in .kdbp/DECISIONS.md.

DecisionWhat it settles
D29/D33provider-switchable verification, mock forbidden in prod; Firebase Admin lazily imported, verify off the event loop.
D35a household is created in exactly one place (complete_setup), idempotent, never auto-created by context loading.
D148consent enforced server-side at setup, gate placement deliberate (post-replay, in-try, claim-discarding); ensure_consent for programmatic callers.
REQ-10SSE auth via query param (EventSource cannot set headers), capped at 4096B; PENDING #30 tracks log suppression.
—The signOut teardown order (cancel → clear → wipe → residue → firebaseSignOut) with the sign-out-storm guard — P37/Phase 56 caching decisions.
C2the redo wizard preloads declared allergens so re-onboarding can never silently wipe them to [].
Deletion orderingDB wipe commits first; Firebase identity delete is post-commit best-effort (self-healing re-provision on failure).
D184hide what you cannot honour: the myopic walk's C4. The repair chosen was to REMOVE the affordance, not to wire it, because there is no join flow to wire it to. The card, its icon, its locale keys and HouseholdModeButton all stay intact and dormant — the same shape RECIPE_CREATION_ENABLED uses — so re-enabling is one flag plus the flow. Flipping it without the flow re-ships the trap, which is why the checklist lives at the flag.

Code Data model

DB entities and API shapes — each names its file and the endpoints that touch it

A field typed with another documented class LINKS to it (violet) instead of repeating its structure. Examples are synthetic — derived from Literal values and field-name heuristics, never real user data.
Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: they count references inside the config-mapped files only, so a zero means no indexed usage — go check, never dead. One unmapped file falsifies a zero; nothing falsifies a count.

About this section

Backend: auth/verifier.py (Firebase verify off-loop, mock lanes, identity delete, boot fail-fast), auth/context.py (AuthContext + bearer/query dependencies), services/setup.py (complete_setup — the one household creator — + preference upserts + the D148 gate), api/setup.py (routes + /me + DELETE /me ordering). Web: auth/AuthProvider.tsx (tri-state, token getter wiring, ordered teardown, 401-storm guard), auth/authContext.ts + auth/useAuth.ts, app/PersistGate.tsx (three-layer isolation) with lib/query/persist.ts + persisterRegistry.ts, features/auth/screens/InitialSetupScreen.tsx + setupMapping.ts + SetupScreen.tsx (wizard + live seams), routes/RequireAuth.tsx + RequireSetup.tsx (guard topology), lib/api/client.ts (terminal-401 side-channel).

Code Data-model candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; the verdict lands in DECISIONS/PENDING via review or a health pass, never here

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — structural twins ≥ 80% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god class ≥ 15 fields (from the N fields flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing uses this" — similarity and size are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped classes sharing 87% of their field names is TRUE no matter what lives outside the map, and a 22-field class is 22 fields however little the config covers. Absence of references is neither — a single file outside the entity config falsifies it. This section names only what the instrument can actually support. The usage evidence lives on the Data model page — two bars per class, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per class only, only above the 50% line, Python only, mapped files only, and only field NAMES (types and semantics are not compared). Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. This TABLE cuts higher still — it lists pairs at ≥ 80%, so the 50% recording floor is what the flag sees, not what you are reading. This page is a FLOOR, not a census: it under-reports duplication and always will. That direction is the safe one — under-reporting a positive signal costs you a missed merge; under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — classes outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can carry near-identical schemas and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

Code Function candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; same contract as the data-model candidates, function-scoped

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — identifier twins ≥ 85% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god function ≥ 50 lines (from the N length flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing calls this" — similarity and length are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped defs sharing 87% of their body identifiers is TRUE regardless of what lies outside the map, and a 120-line function is 120 lines however little the config covers. "Nothing references this" is falsified by one file outside the corpus — so this section names duplication and size, and never asserts deadness. The usage evidence lives on the Functions page — two bars per def, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per def, only among defs with ≥ 8 body identifiers, only above the 60% line, Python only, mapped files only — while this TABLE cuts higher still, listing pairs at ≥ 85%. Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. The page is a FLOOR, not a census — and that direction is the safe one: under-reporting a positive signal costs a missed merge, while under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — files outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can share dozens of byte-identical functions and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

Verified by — no spec pointer joins the corpus record (the manifest names no captured test file).

What this set shows: The first setup step used to offer two household cards side by side: create one, or join a partner's with an invitation. Choosing the invitation produced exactly the same request as creating — so someone who thought they were joining a shared kitchen quietly got their own empty one. The founder ruling was to hide the card until a real join flow exists. This shot is that step rendered afterwards.

Risk Not carried forward

claims the legacy pages made that this page refuses to repeat, and why

  • "consent is a client-side gate" (pre-D148 reading) — dropped: the client ConsentGate is the happy path only; the enforcement is the service-side 409, placed after replay and inside the try so a rejection cannot poison the idempotency key.
  • "the setup 409 means a conflict" — qualified: three distinct 409s share the status at this boundary (setup-in-progress, consent-required, setup-required) — the detail string, not the code, is the contract.
  • "0 web unit tests for auth" (ranking-era signal) — dropped: the web carries the estate's headline safety tests here (PersistGate cross-user isolation, the signOut teardown order, the terminal-401 storm guard, persist resilience — 37 claimed cases).
